searchText: Does anyone dare an estimate where we are with 4844 stability, maybe measured with terms of software release types? Can we already call this (all specs bundled) a **release candidate**? Or are we still more in **alpha** or **beta** stage? 🙂 I know this question is highly subjective but I find it nevertheless meaningful since changes on 4844 specs where so heavy during the last weeks and I have lost a bit my intuition if this will go on an on or if we are rather stablizing. How to interpret `excess_data_gas`? Is this just a param to compute data gas price? Because it is not `data_gas_used - target`, isn't it? <@393119312350543872> are you working on more state tests for 4844? It's ~~indeed ~~ `max(excess_data_gas + data_gas_used - target, 0)`. But calculated using parent block's `data_gas_used` and `excess_data_gas ` Yes, some merged already. Nimbus client implemented 4844 For data gas used and excess data gas need more tests though. I just did basics blobtx checks I used tests from ethereum/tests by <@393119312350543872> (🙏 ) to implement `BLOBHASH` and blob transactions validation. But some things seem horrible wrong in the implementation so tests cases are still missing. https://github.com/ethereum/evmone/pull/668 Which things? This tests are based on nimbus if you find implementation issue difference to the specs, lets investigate `excess_data_gas` aggregates over blocks. The `data_gas_used` is a param which stores how much data gas is used (this scales with the amount of blobs per block) Currently the target blobs are 3 and the max blobs per block are 6. If a block has more blobs than the target blobs, the excessDataGas will increase. If it has less blobs than target blobs, it will decrease. (I think the data gas used in the header is to ensure that as a header verifier you do not need to download all txs, you can just take previous header and then calculate the excess data gas)
